10. To explain it further, Mr. Shafiq Ahmed, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, has submitted that the remedy for termination under section 19(1) is either a complaint under section 25 of the Employment of Labour (Standing Orders) Act.1965 or alternatively under section 34 of the Industrial Relations Ordinance, 1969. But in the instant case the respondent sent the grievance petition to the petitioner under section: 25(l) of the Employment of Labour (Standing Orders) Act. 1965, but while making a claim before the Labour Court he filed it under section 15(2) of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 which, according to him, is not maintainable. He further claims that the respondent No.1 filed the application under section 15(2) of the Payment of Wages Act only with a malafide intention of avoiding the limitation period of thirty days under the Standing Orders Act. 

 11. On the other hand, while admitting that he was terminated under section 19(1) of the Standing Orders Act, the respondent No.1 submits that he had to file an application under section 15(2) of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 to recover the gratuity to which he is entitled under the Memorandum of Agreement but was denied of it at the time of final payment made to him. It is only under this section a claim can be lodged to the Labour Court for any deduction made in the payment of wages. He further claims that he is not challenging the termination itself he is only claiming what is due to him by way of gratuity. Therefore, there is no bar for him to come under section 15(2) of the Payment of Wages Act. He does not also deny that he had signed a statement to the effect that he had received full payment from the petitioner company but claims that payment of gratuity is still subsisting under section 23 of the Payment of Wages Act. The said section provides that any contract or agreement whether made before or after the commencement of this Act, whereby an employed person relinquishes any right conferred by this Act shall be null and void insofar as it purports to deprive him of such right. Lastly, the period of limitation for filing a complaint under section 15(2) of the Payment of Wages Act is 6 months and he has filed the complaint case well within that period. He was terminated on 31-12-92, received full payment on 11-1-93, sent his grievance petition on 17-1-93 and filed the case under section 15(2) on 25-2-93. Therefore, the case was filed within the limitation period. 

 31. On the other hand, the Employment of Labour (Standing Orders) Act, 1965 and the Industrial Relations Ordinance regulate conditions of service of workers employed in shops and commercial and industrial establishments and for matters connected therein and provide the law relating to the formation of trade unions, the relation between employers and workmen and the avoidance .and settlement of any difference or disputes arising between them. Apparently, the object and purpose of the Payment of Wages Act and the objects and purpose of the Employment of Labour (Standing Orders) Act and the Industrial Relations Ordinance are not in parimeteria. Their fundamentals are completely different in nature. Considering the objects of the Standing Orders Act and the Industrial Relations Ordinance, the respondent No. 1 cannot seek relief under the Payment of Wages Act, for the claim arising out of Standing Orders Act The respondent No.1, on being terminated under section 19 of the Standing Orders Act, should have sought relief either under section 25 of that Act or alternatively under section 34 of the Industrial Relations Ordinance. He should not have sought relief under section 15(2) of the Payment of Wages Act as that will cause much anomaly. Once it is allowed the aggrieved persons mostly will come under: section 15(2) of the Payment of Wages Act to avail of a larger period of limitation that was definitely not the intendment behind the enactment of me Act. Therefore, we are unable to accede to me claim that the respondent No.1 in the instant case is entitled to claim relief under section 15(2) of the Payment of Wages Act. His substantive right lies under section 19(1) and me procedural right for the same lies under section 25 of the Employment of Labour (Standing Orders).  Act 1965 or under section 34 of the Industrial Relations Ordinance. For being a terminated worker under section 19 of the Standing Orders Act the respondent No. 1 can claim wages for 120 days if no notice is given before terminating him and compensation at the rate of 30 days' wages for every completed year of .service or for any part thereof in excess of six months in addition to any other benefit' to which he may be entitled under this Act or any other law for the time being in force.
